fields.description:
Register the `bridge` noun and its subcommand dispatch, so the redesigned surface exists for the
sibling tickets to attach verbs to.

    rebar bridge setup | check-access | fsck | status | preview | sync | pause | resume

**This ticket was SPLIT on 2026-08-07** (see the split comment). It previously also owned the three
verb retirements and the three verb renames; four plan-review rounds produced 2 -> 7 -> 4 -> 7
blocking findings without converging, because each verb dragged an unenumerated consumer set. Those
now live in their own tickets:
* `c61a-9f8f-8ef9-4601` — retire the two DEAD verbs (`bridge-status`, `purge-bridge`). Independent;
  no dependency on this ticket.
* `4a44-4abb-ae91-4e51` — retire `reconcile` and the `--mode` flag (CLI + engine). `depends_on` this.
* `e27c-5a20-cd13-43b2` — rename the three SURVIVING verbs (`bridge-fsck` -> `bridge fsck`,
  `bridge-probe` -> `bridge check-access`, `jira-onboard` -> `bridge setup`). `depends_on` this.

What remains here is the surface itself: the noun, the dispatch table, and the two verbs that have
no predecessor to rename from — `preview` and `sync`.

## Why this ticket is the root of the epic

Six siblings already `depends_on` it — `1104-93eb-6ce0-4a19`, `424f-bc35-b7ca-419a`,
`030f-c14f-596a-4f79`, `b69c-5787-81b8-4052`, `9895-aa2c-8907-4db6`, `f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d` — and
that edge is exactly right: they attach their verbs to the surface this ticket creates. Keeping the
surface registration separate from any single verb's consumer migration is what makes each of those
reviewable on its own.

## `preview` and `sync` are the read/write knob

`bridge preview` reads and reports; `bridge sync` mutates. There is no `--mode` here and no
inverted default: `bridge sync` with no arguments MUTATES. (That is precisely why sibling
`4a44-4abb-ae91-4e51` retires `reconcile` with NO alias — `rebar reconcile` with no arguments meant
dry-run, so an alias would be a silent behaviour change.)

Flags survive only if their help text can be written without internals. Ten candidates reduced to
three: `--max-changes N`, `--only <ids>`, `--except <ids>`, `--max-age <duration>`, plus the house
`--output json`. Maintainer decision: `--only`/`--except` limit what is EXAMINED as well as what is
changed (unlike the internal `--filter-local-ids` they replace, which filtered only writes and was
marked "for validation use only" for that reason), and preview/sync remains the read/write knob.

## B4 — `mode.py` SURVIVES this ticket and the whole surface work

`mode.py` is not deleted anywhere in this ticket's scope. Two live consumers keep `MODE_CAPS` and
the `Mode` rank ladder alive:
* the **MCP surface** gates mutating runs on `MODE_CAPS[parsed] != 0`
  (`_mcp_reads.py:41,286,291`), and that surface is retired by sibling `f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d`;
* the **phase gate** ranks by `Mode` and — per sibling `1104-93eb-6ce0-4a19`'s decision — its pause
  compatibility value must remain a REAL `Mode` member (`gated_mode: "reconcile-check"`), because a
  non-`Mode` shim makes `_mode_blocks` swallow the `ValueError` and silently fail OPEN.
So `mode.py` survives with its table and ladder intact; its eventual disposition belongs to `f789`
and `1104`. Deleting it here would break both.

## B1 — cross-verb functional assertions are SCOPED, because the edge cannot be added

The pause/resume/status behavioural chain needs state owned by `1104-93eb-6ce0-4a19`
(remote-persisted pause) and `b69c-5787-81b8-4052` (durable status). An edge from this ticket to
either would be a CYCLE — both already `depends_on` this one, since they attach their verbs to the
surface it creates. So this ticket proves only what it alone owns; the behavioural assertions
belong to the sibling that builds the state.

## The BRIDGE health verb is `bridge fsck` — top-level `rebar doctor` is PRESERVED (B2/B7)

No `bridge doctor` spelling or alias ships. This is scoped to the bridge surface ONLY: the existing
top-level `rebar doctor` — the store link-repair diagnostic dispatched at
`src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:323`, unrelated to the Jira bridge — is PRESERVED untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar bridge <verb>` exists and dispatches for the agreed verb set; `bridge` appears in
      `rebar --help`, and `rebar bridge` with no verb prints the verb list rather than erroring
      opaquely
- [ ] An unknown `rebar bridge <nonsense>` fails with a usage message naming the valid verbs, and
      does NOT fall through to any top-level subcommand
- [ ] Each verb this ticket OWNS is proven to FUNCTION, not merely to exist: `bridge preview`
      performs no Jira write and no ticket-event write (asserted against a store snapshot taken
      before and after the run), and `bridge sync` mutates
- [ ] `pause`, `resume` and `status` are proven only to EXIST and dispatch here; their behavioural
      assertions belong to `1104-93eb-6ce0-4a19` and `b69c-5787-81b8-4052` respectively, which own
      the underlying state and already depend on this ticket — an edge back would be a cycle (B1)
- [ ] `setup`, `check-access` and `fsck` are proven only to EXIST and dispatch here; their behaviour
      and consumer migration belong to `e27c-5a20-cd13-43b2`
- [ ] Every shipped flag's help text contains no internals (no "mode", "rank", "gate", "lock",
      "cap", "pass", "binding store", no exit-code numbers)
- [ ] `mode.py`'s `MODE_CAPS` table and `Mode` ladder still exist and are still consumed at the end
      of this ticket; a test asserts the phase gate can still round-trip
      `gated_mode: "reconcile-check"` as a real `Mode` member (B4)
- [ ] The BRIDGE health verb is spelled `bridge fsck`; no `bridge doctor` spelling or alias ships
      (B2/B7). The existing top-level `rebar doctor` store link-repair command
      (`_cli/__init__.py:323`) is untouched, and a test asserts `rebar doctor` still dispatches
      after this ticket
- [ ] `docs/user-guide.md` and `docs/cli-reference.md` document the `bridge` noun and its verb set
fields.title: Establish the bridge verb group (noun + subcommand dispatch)
